Measurements and limitations

All 483 visible footprints remain: 468 complete engineering quads and 15 clipped partials. The previous 483 delivered footprints are available in blue. All 496 original masks, nine linked fragments and four frame-support hypotheses remain accessible. No supplied layout or module map is used.

Eleven additional shared contacts now use one inferred common engineering seam per pair. Together with four earlier repairs, fifteen contact seams retain 546 observed white intervals as optional magenta support. In 232 intervals, white reaches an endpoint of the sampling corridor; these show only the observed portion, not the complete physical band width or a calibrated confidence region. Visible gaps retain separate edges; no fixed pitch or gap is imposed. All 40,479 pair intersection areas across these public images are non-increasing. Material conflicts fall from twelve to one; this threshold means an intersection exceeding 1% of the smaller footprint. Forty-five positive-area pairs remain, including small and numerical intersections. The remaining material pair is two clipped source-edge fragments with a 3 px² overlap.

Full-quad matches change from 468/468/316 to 468/468/317; partials are not counted as full rectangles. All 483 references, including fifteen partials, remain in the denominator. No previously matched reference is lost at these thresholds.

Of 468 paired complete modules, sixteen improve corner RMSE, six worsen and 446 are unchanged. The largest RMSE increase is 0.069 px. One image's boundary p95 increases by approximately 0.000053 px; other aggregate border changes are favorable or unchanged. These are exposed development comparisons against approximate author references, not physical metrology, independent validation or a production-default change.

The tiny remaining pair's inherited side angle prevents the original source sampler from running. A separately tested native-body-axis seed finds only three usable white-band profiles and still abstains under the unchanged evidence requirement. No output or threshold was forced to achieve zero conflicts. Source-edge uncertainty and residual top/bottom fit errors remain.
